intent: Compare the interest rates at the short-term and long-term maturities for the normal and inverted yield curve scenarios to determine the direction of the slope in each case.

requirements.question: Are all required line series shown in every declared panel?
What is the direction of the slope for the normal yield curve scenario?
What is the direction of the slope for the inverted yield curve scenario?

units.claim: All 2 required series appear in panel single chart.
accept: every required series is visible and correctly labeled in this panel
reject: series assigned to the wrong panel

units.claim: For the normal yield curve, the interest rate increases from the short-term maturity (3m) to the long-term maturity (10y), indicating an upward slope.
units.computation: Compare values at 3m (0.2667) and 10y (0.8444); 0.8444 > 0.2667, so the slope is upward.
accept: Normal yield curve rises from 3m to 10y
reject: Normal yield curve falls from 3m to 10y

units.claim: For the inverted yield curve, the interest rate decreases from the short-term maturity (3m) to the long-term maturity (10y), indicating a downward slope.
units.computation: Compare values at 3m (0.6444) and 10y (0.1778); 0.1778 < 0.6444, so the slope is downward.
accept: Inverted yield curve falls from 3m to 10y
reject: Inverted yield curve rises from 3m to 10y

optional_valid: Mention that the normal curve starts lower than the inverted curve at 3m and ends higher at 10y.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal explanations for why the curves have these shapes.
Intermediate maturities not present in the table.
Absolute differences or percentage changes as separate claims beyond slope direction.
review_notes: Only two maturities (3m and 10y) are available per scenario; slope direction is determined by comparing these endpoints.
No cross-panel comparison is needed because panel_count is 1.
